# Small-hole asymptotics of the zero-flux ring branch

Generated by `scripts/ring_asymptotics.py` from `results/hires/rings_merged.json` (rings with r_h <= 0.0393) and `results/hires/branch.json` (bubbles).

Law tested: X_ring(r_h) = X_bubble(z_pole = r_h log(1/r_h)) + O(r_h) for X = We, λ, |Γ| (|Γ| is compared with 2φ_pole of the bubble).

## Leading coefficient from the rings

123 rings, r_h = 8.636e-06 … 0.03924 (z_eff = 0.0001 … 0.1271).

D_X = (X_ring − X_bubble(z_eff))/r_h is fitted by dA·log(1/r_h) + B + C·r_h log(1/r_h) [+ E·r_h]; the ring value of the leading coefficient is X'(0) + dA.

This absolute least-squares fit is dominated by the largest holes, where We − We* is largest; the window fits above are the sharp test.
